name: Sanlitun
tagline: Embassy district bars, malls and the best coffee
description: Sanlitun sits in Chaoyang between the embassy compounds and the Taikoo Li malls, a grid of wide leafy avenues and back lanes packed with third-wave coffee bars, craft beer taps and international restaurants. It holds most of Beijing's foreign residents, so English signage and serviced apartments are everywhere.
bestFor: Nomads who want an easy landing pad with English-speaking services and nightlife on the doorstep
pros: Densest cluster of laptop-friendly cafes in the city
Walkable to two subway lines and dozens of restaurants
Easiest area to rent short-term without Mandarin
cons: The most expensive rent per square metre in Beijing
Bar street noise runs late on weekends
Feels like an expat bubble rather than real Beijing

name: Gulou and the Drum Tower hutongs
tagline: Grey-brick alleys, courtyard houses and indie cafes
description: The lanes around the Drum and Bell Towers in Dongcheng are single-storey grey-brick hutongs where courtyard homes have been converted into record shops, tiny roasters and live music bars. Old residents play cards in the alley while young Beijingers cycle through. It is the most atmospheric place to live in the city.
bestFor: Creatives and long-stay nomads who want character over convenience
pros: Genuinely beautiful, bikeable old Beijing streets
Strong independent cafe and music scene
Central, close to Houhai lake and the subway
cons: Many courtyard rooms have shared or public toilets
Poor insulation makes winters cold and summers hot
Tourist crowds on the main lanes at weekends

name: Guomao CBD
tagline: Glass towers, coworking and metro connections
description: Guomao is Beijing's central business district, a cluster of glass towers around the CCTV building and the China World complex. Streets are wide and corporate rather than charming, but this is where the serviced offices, coworking floors, gyms and international hotels are. Two subway lines cross here.
bestFor: Remote workers who want a proper desk, fast fibre and client meeting space
pros: Best coworking and serviced-office supply in Beijing
Modern apartments with reliable heating and lifts
cons: Sterile after office hours and on weekends
Rents match Sanlitun without the atmosphere
Heavy traffic on the East Third Ring Road

name: Wudaokou
tagline: Student Beijing, cheap food and late-night noodles
description: Wudaokou sits in Haidian between Tsinghua and Peking universities, so the streets are full of students, cheap canteens, Korean barbecue joints and 24-hour study cafes. Rents drop sharply compared to Chaoyang, and the area is well served by Line 13. Green campus space is a short walk away.
bestFor: Budget nomads and anyone studying Mandarin alongside remote work
pros: Much cheaper rent and food than east Beijing
Big international student community, easy to meet people
Cafes open late and tolerate long laptop sessions
cons: Around 12 km from the Sanlitun and CBD social scene
Crowded and noisy during term time
Older housing stock with variable maintenance

name: Wangjing
tagline: Quiet high-rise suburb with a Korean core
description: Wangjing is a planned district of newer residential towers in northeast Chaoyang, home to Beijing's largest Korean community and to tech offices including Alibaba and Meituan. Streets are wide with real greenery, supermarkets and family amenities, and apartments are newer and larger than anything central.
bestFor: Nomads staying months who want space, quiet and a normal daily routine
pros: Newer, larger flats for noticeably less money
Excellent Korean food and grocery options
Calmer air and more parks than the inner ring roads
cons: Roughly a 40 minute subway ride to central sights
Limited nightlife beyond restaurants and bars
Very little English spoken outside Korean businesses
